{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Make a pattern that repeats with no visible edge: place the tile next to itself, left, right, up or down, and the motifs carry on across the join. Seamless Tile Pixaroma makes Krea 2 draw it that way, and Seamless Preview Pixaroma shows it repeated and checks the edges. Use it for fabric and wallpaper prints, gift wrap, backgrounds and textures for games and 3D. Krea 2 follows long, detailed prompts well, which suits prints with several kinds of motifs.

 Steps

  1. Describe your pattern in Prompt Pixaroma (1).
  2. Pick the size of one tile on Sizes Pixaroma (2). 1536 x 1536 is Krea 2's best size for patterns.
  3. Leave the seed (3) on F to repeat a pattern, or switch it to R for a new one each Run.
  4. Leave Seamless Tile Pixaroma (4) on Both for a pattern that repeats in every direction. Left and right or Up and down join only one pair of edges (a border, a strip); Off makes a normal picture.
  5. Press Run. Seamless Preview Pixaroma shows the tile repeated 2x2 and checks the edges; Save Image Pixaroma saves the tile itself, the file you repeat in other apps (or the repeated pattern: see What to save below).

 Writing a pattern prompt

  • Prints (fabric, wallpaper, gift wrap): start with A flat surface pattern design of ... and name the kind of print: a chintz, a toile, a damask, a ditsy floral, a folk-art print, a block print.
  • Textures for games and 3D: start with A texture of ... and add seen straight from above in flat, even light, so no corner is darker than the rest.
  • Name the motifs and how they are drawn, 3 or 4 colours and ONE background colour, and end with ... fill the whole surface evenly. The demo prompt is written this way.
  • You do not need the word seamless: Seamless Tile Pixaroma makes the edges join whatever the prompt says.
  • Want help with the words? Workflows 5, 6 and 7 use AI Prompt Pixaroma to write the prompt for you: 5 from a picture of a pattern you like, 6 from a few words, 7 from many ideas in one Run.

 Good to know

  • At 1536 x 1536 the motifs come out at a natural size; at 1024 x 1024 they came out smaller in our tests.
  • In our tests Krea 2 was best at floral and botanical prints like the demo. Small motifs that are all the same size (bunnies, stars) tended to line up in rows.
  • Krea 2's license allows commercial use only while your company earns under US$1 million a year (see Download Models). Workflow 2 uses Z-Image, an Apache 2.0 model, free for any use.
  • The seam check on Seamless Preview: PASS means no line where the edges meet. It checks the join, not the picture, so look at the repeat too, for a line or a block the tile itself draws. WARN can be a line of the pattern itself that happens to sit on the edge, like a joint between two planks or tiles: click the view row on Seamless Preview (it shows 2x2), pick Offset, which puts the corners in the middle, and look. FAIL means a visible line. That is expected with Seamless Tile on Off, and on the edges you did not pick with Left and right or Up and down. On Both, check that VAE Decode takes its VAE from Seamless Tile Pixaroma.
  • Long straight diagonal stripes across the whole tile (candy cane, pinstripes) join at the edge but bend or break halfway: the model cannot count how many stripes fit. Horizontal and vertical stripes, plaid, chevrons, waves and tossed motifs come out clean.
  • What to save: Switch Pixaroma before Save Image picks it. Tile (the default) saves one tile, the file you repeat in other apps for prints, fabric or games. Repeated pattern saves the tile repeated the way Seamless Preview's view shows it (2x2, 3x3, Offset...), to show or share the pattern: a bigger picture, 3072 x 3072 for a 1536 tile in the 2x2 view. Click a row's toggle to pick it.
  • Saving for print? Click the gear on Save Image Pixaroma and turn on Print resolution (300 ppi). The pixels stay the same, but the PNG or JPG says 300 ppi, so print apps open it at print size: a 1536 px tile is about 13 cm (5.1 in) wide. Off, apps read it as 72 ppi, for screens.
  • Model Attention Backend makes the render 12 to 14 % faster with the same patterns in our tests. It needs an Nvidia or AMD card; on any other it uses the normal attention by itself.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones (and an orange one whose model file sits in another folder on your PC).

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note. Shown as missing, but you have the file in another folder? Click the model name on the node and pick it.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Krea 2 Turbo) - The image model, Krea 2 Turbo from Krea: 8 steps, CFG 1. It understands long, detailed prompts well, so it is the best one here for prints with several motifs.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 4B, reads the prompt) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something the image model understands.
  • Load VAE (Qwen Image VAE) - Turns the finished render into a picture you can see, and a picture into the model's own format.

 The steps you set

Blue. These are the only nodes you need to touch; the numbered ones are the steps in How to Use.

  • Prompt Pixaroma (1. your pattern) - The prompt box. Describe the pattern, not a scene: the motifs, how they are drawn, the colours and the background. The How to Use note shows how.
  • Sizes Pixaroma (2. tile size) - The size of ONE tile. 1536 x 1536, 1024 x 1024, 1536 x 1024. The Portrait / Landscape switch turns the wide one on its side.
  • Seed Pixaroma (3. fixed or random) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same pattern every Run, R (random) a new one each Run. The demo uses seed 3.
  • Seamless Tile Pixaroma (4. which edges join) - Makes the model draw a picture whose edges join: put it next to itself and you see no line. Both joins every edge (patterns, textures), Left and right or Up and down only one pair, Off makes a normal picture. It changes the model AND the VAE, so the VAE Decode takes the VAE from this node.
  • Switch Pixaroma (what to save) - Picks what Save Image saves. Tile: one tile, the file you repeat in other apps (print, fabric, games). Repeated pattern: the tile repeated the way Seamless Preview's view shows it (2x2, 3x3, Offset...), to show or share the pattern. Click a row's toggle to pick it.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • Krea2 Enhancer Pixaroma (sharper detail) - Gives Krea 2 sharper, bolder detail. On at 0.1, the setting of our Krea 2 workflows. The edges still join with it on.
  • Model Attention Backend (faster attention) - Switches the model to Comfy Kitchen's faster attention. In our tests the patterns looked the same and the render was 12 to 14 % faster. It is a core ComfyUI node; on a card where it is not available it falls back to the normal attention by itself.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • CLIP Text Encode (reads the prompt) - Reads the prompt through the text encoder.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. Krea 2 Turbo runs at CFG 1, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • Empty SD3 Latent Image (blank canvas) - The blank canvas the picture is painted on, at the size it receives from Sizes Pixaroma.
  • KSampler (8 steps) - The render: 8 steps, CFG 1, er_sde, simple, the settings of our Krea 2 workflows.
  • VAE Decode (uses the Seamless Tile VAE) - Turns the finished render into a picture. Its VAE comes from Seamless Tile Pixaroma: a plain VAE would leave a faint line at the edges.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Seamless Preview Pixaroma (the repeat + seam check) - Shows the picture repeated, so you can see how the pattern looks as wallpaper or fabric, and checks the edges: PASS means no line where the edges meet. Click its view row (it shows 2x2) to see it as 3x3, Offset (the corners meet in the middle), Half-drop or Half-brick.
  • Save Image Pixaroma (saves what you picked) - Saves every picture to the folder and file name you set, and shows them on the node. %input% in the name becomes the wired name, so each result keeps the name of its picture. An empty folder box means ComfyUI's own output folder; a / in the name makes a subfolder.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the number of pictures and their size.

Tile sizeTime
1536 x 1536 (the demo)about 13 s
1536 x 1024, wide or tallabout 9 s
1024 x 1024about 6 s

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models from disk (Krea 2 and its text encoder, about 18 GB together), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

 On a 16 GB card

Two testers timed these workflows on 16 GB cards:

  • A 1536 x 1536 tile took about 45 s on every Run on an RTX 4060 Ti with 32 GB of RAM, and about 20 s on an RTX 5080 with 64 GB of RAM. Krea 2 and its text encoder (about 18 GB together) do not both fit in 16 GB.

 On an 8 GB card

A tester timed it on an RTX 4070 Laptop (8 GB) with 32 GB of RAM: a 1536 x 1536 tile took about 1 min 20 s.

nodes.title: READ ME: border corners
widgets_values:
BORDER CORNERS (stage 2, below)

Prompt 1 is just the border's STYLE. Two Text Join nodes turn it into the strip prompt (stage 1) and the corner prompt (stage 2).

1. Stage 1 makes the border strip (Seamless Tile: Left and right).
2. Seamless Border Prep turns the corner where the pattern mirrors itself (corner_at: Mirror line), lays it out as a mitre (45 degree join) and masks a band along the diagonal (repaint: Seam).
3. The corner KSampler paints an ornament on the turn with the model WITHOUT Seamless Tile (denoise 0.8).
4. Seamless Border Kit puts the strip's own pixels back outside the seam and joins everything exactly.

Two frames come out: the painted one and, on the right, the mitred one with no model. On the mirror line the mitre alone often looks like a designed corner; keep whichever you like.

Tips:
- Like the strip? Set Seed to fixed; the corner sampler re-rolls on every run.
- Keep the corner prompt free of 'diagonal', 'tiled' or 'meet': those make the model draw a line along the join.
- Denoise 0.9 and up can paint a bar along the diagonal; 0.7 stays close to the mitre.
- seam_width 0.25 = a small ornament; 0.4 (default here) = room for a bigger one.
- Keep blend low (8-16): a high blend fades the strip into the corner.
